Monte McNair :: Career :: Houston Rockets :: chunk_0001
In 2007, McNair joined the [Houston Rockets](/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") as the basketball operations senior analyst. McNair was then promoted to director of basketball operations in 2013, VP of basketball operations in 2016, and assistant GM in 2018. While working for the Rockets team, his organization reached the [NBA playoffs](/wiki/NBA_playoffs "NBA playoffs") for eight consecutive years, including two [Western Conference Finals](/wiki/NBA_Conference_Finals "NBA Conference Finals") appearances.[[4]](#cite_note-4) Highly regarded executive [Daryl Morey](/wiki/Daryl_Morey "Daryl Morey") (who was the president of basketball operations of the Rockets at this time) said in 2018, "Monte has been absolutely critical to the success of the Rockets over his long tenure."

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/New7Wonders.jpg/500px-New7Wonders.jpg)](/wiki/File:New7Wonders.jpg)

From left to right, top to bottom: [Chichén Itzá](/wiki/Chich%C3%A9n_Itz%C3%A1 "Chichén Itzá"), *[Christ the Redeemer](/wiki/Christ_the_Redeemer_(statue) "Christ the Redeemer (statue)")*, the [Great Wall of China](/wiki/Great_Wall_of_China "Great Wall of China"), [Machu Picchu](/wiki/Machu_Picchu "Machu Picchu"), [Petra](/wiki/Petra "Petra"), the [Taj Mahal](/wiki/Taj_Mahal "Taj Mahal"), and the [Colosseum](/wiki/Colosseum "Colosseum")

The **New 7 Wonders of the World** was a campaign started in 2001 to choose [Wonders of the World](/wiki/Wonders_of_the_World "Wonders of the World") from a selection of 200 existing monuments.[[1]](#cite_note-1) The popularity poll via free web-based voting and telephone voting was led by Canadian-Swiss Bernard Weber[[2]](#cite_note-2) and organized by the New 7 Wonders Foundation (N7W) based in Zurich, Switzerland, with winners announced on 7 July 2007 at [Estádio da Luz](/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_da_Luz "Estádio da Luz") in [Lisbon](/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon").[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-nwVFC-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6) The poll was considered unscientific partly because it was possible for people to cast multiple votes.[[7]](#cite_note-LAT-7) According to [John Zogby](/wiki/John_Zogby "John Zogby"), founder and current President/CEO of the US polling organization [Zogby International](/wiki/Zogby_International "Zogby International"), New 7 Wonders Foundation drove "the largest poll on record".[[5]](#cite_note-nwVFC-5)

The **flag of the U.S. state of Iowa** is a vertical tricolor flag designed by [Dixie Cornell Gebhardt](/wiki/Dixie_Cornell_Gebhardt "Dixie Cornell Gebhardt") in 1917. Iowa legislators officially adopted the flag in 1921.

It is one of nine U.S. state flags to feature an eagle, alongside those of [Illinois](/wiki/Flag_of_Illinois "Flag of Illinois"), [Michigan](/wiki/Flag_of_Michigan "Flag of Michigan"), [Missouri](/wiki/Flag_of_Missouri "Flag of Missouri"), [New York](/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_New_York "Coat of arms of New York"), [North Dakota](/wiki/Flag_of_North_Dakota "Flag of North Dakota"), [Oregon](/wiki/Flag_of_Oregon "Flag of Oregon"), [Pennsylvania](/wiki/Flag_of_Pennsylvania "Flag of Pennsylvania") and [Wyoming](/wiki/Flag_of_Wyoming "Flag of Wyoming"). The eagle carrying streamers in its beak also features on the Iowa state seal.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

fanoutqa_012839.x:
Robert Burns Woodward :: Early life and education :: chunk_0001
Woodward was born in [Boston, Massachusetts](/wiki/Boston,_Massachusetts "Boston, Massachusetts"), on April 10, 1917. He was the son of Margaret Burns (an immigrant from Scotland who claimed to be a descendant of the poet, [Robert Burns](/wiki/Robert_Burns "Robert Burns")) and her husband, Arthur Chester Woodward, himself the son of [Roxbury](/wiki/Roxbury,_Boston "Roxbury, Boston") apothecary, Harlow Elliot Woodward.

His father was one of the many victims of the [1918 influenza pandemic](/wiki/1918_influenza_pandemic "1918 influenza pandemic").

From a very early age, Woodward was attracted to and engaged in private study of [chemistry](/wiki/Chemistry "Chemistry") while he attended a public primary school, and then [Quincy High School](/wiki/Quincy_High_School_(Massachusetts) "Quincy High School (Massachusetts)"),[[4]](#cite_note-4) in [Quincy, Massachusetts](/wiki/Quincy,_Massachusetts "Quincy, Massachusetts"). By the time he entered high school, he had already managed to perform most of the experiments in [Ludwig Gattermann](/wiki/Ludwig_Gattermann "Ludwig Gattermann")'s then widely used textbook of experimental organic chemistry. In 1928, Woodward contacted the Consul-General of the German consulate in Boston (Baron von Tippelskirch[[5]](#cite_note-halford-5)), and through him, managed to obtain copies of a few original papers published in German journals. Later, in his Cope lecture, he recalled how he had been fascinated when, among these papers, he chanced upon Diels and Alder's original communication about the [Diels–Alder reaction](/wiki/Diels%E2%80%93Alder_reaction "Diels–Alder reaction"). Throughout his career, Woodward was to repeatedly and powerfully use and investigate this reaction, both in theoretical and experimental ways.

[Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"), with a $55.67 billion endowment as of FY2025, is the wealthiest university in the world.

Many colleges and universities in the United States maintain a [financial endowment](/wiki/Financial_endowment "Financial endowment") consisting of [assets](/wiki/Asset "Asset") that are invested in [financial securities](/wiki/Security_(finance) "Security (finance)"), [real estate](/wiki/Real_estate "Real estate"), and other instruments. The investment yields a [return](/wiki/Return_on_investment "Return on investment") that funds a portion of an institution's [operational expenses](/wiki/Operating_expense "Operating expense") while the principal exists in [perpetuity](/wiki/Perpetuity "Perpetuity"). U.S. colleges and universities maintain some of the largest endowments in the world and [make up the vast majority](/wiki/Lists_of_institutions_of_higher_education_by_endowment_size "Lists of institutions of higher education by endowment size") of higher education institutions with endowments greater than $1 billion.

The National Association of College and University Business Officers (NACUBO) maintains information on endowments at U.S. higher education institutions by [fiscal year](/wiki/Fiscal_year "Fiscal year") (FY).[[1]](#cite_note-NACUBOhistoric-1) As of FY2024, the total endowment market value of U.S. institutions stood at $837.720 billion, with an average across all institutions of $1.322 billion and a median of $244.426 million.[[2]](#cite_note-NACUBOtotal-2)[[3]](#cite_note-NACUBO-3)

Ball upset during a game in 2018

On July 17, 2018, Ball underwent an [arthroscopic surgery](/wiki/Arthroscopic_surgery "Arthroscopic surgery") on his left knee to repair a torn [meniscus](/wiki/Meniscus_(anatomy) "Meniscus (anatomy)").[[78]](#cite_note-78) During the offseason, the Lakers signed the four-time [NBA Most Valuable Player](/wiki/NBA_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA Most Valuable Player") LeBron James, which shifted the spotlight away from Ball.[[76]](#cite_note-oram_12242018-76) They also signed veteran point guard [Rajon Rondo](/wiki/Rajon_Rondo "Rajon Rondo") to mentor and compete with the youngster. A week before camp, Lakers coach [Luke Walton](/wiki/Luke_Walton "Luke Walton") stated that Ball would be eased back and not participate in full-contact practices initially.[[75]](#cite_note-youngmisuk_09192018-75)

Ball's added bulk made him better on defense,[[6]](#cite_note-cacciola_12252018-6) and he became one of the Lakers' most dynamic defenders during the season as he picked up point guards full-court to create turnovers in the backcourt.[[76]](#cite_note-oram_12242018-76) On offense, he had to adjust to playing off the ball more with James often handling the ball.[[76]](#cite_note-oram_12242018-76)[[79]](#cite_note-79) On December 15, in a 128–100 win against the [Charlotte Hornets](/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets"), the duo became the first teammates to achieve a triple-double in the same game since [Jason Kidd](/wiki/Jason_Kidd "Jason Kidd") and [Vince Carter](/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter") did it in 2007, with Ball posting 16 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists, while James had 24 points, 12 rebounds, and 11 assists. As of 2017, an estimated 44,525,458 residents of the United States were foreign-born,[[274]](#cite_note-factfinder.census.gov/faces-288) 13.5% of the country's total population. This demographic includes recent as well as longstanding immigrants; statistically Europeans have resided in the US longer than those from other regions with approximately 66% having arrived prior to 2000.[[275]](#cite_note-289)
